column8: Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the paper half of why signed as well as held (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5 cites FAS 116 para 6, now ASC 958-605-25-8): the books test that a promise was made, never whether she can pay; read in FASB's own PDF and two codification copies.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d store, one clause beside Q200-008 at most: the books count a legal right nobody plans to use, so the Treasuries, not the right to sue, make her figure paid; two unofficial codification copies.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the reason her letter carries no way to withdraw (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5, Left out): a stated exit turns a promise into an intention a gift office does not count; her flexibility already sits outside the figure (IPS l.15).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the letter's verb: I promise to give, never intend or plan; the report may still say pledge letter (CASE, Q200-001), and Q18-004 holds the commitment words.

Sun 22 Nov: store, or one clause under row 1: the paper rule guards against a promise never made, not a giver who cannot pay; the second guard is her Treasuries (Keel reading of the Board's stated purpose).

Sun 22 Nov: store, a judge's-question line behind aha 8: the standard draws the promise line at words, its one dissenter at the chance of cash; a dissent, never the rule, and at most a clause in 3d's tight budget.
Sun 22 Nov: store; a promise to give is one-way, which is why courts reach for reliance (Q99 rows 15-20); her payment needs only the Treasuries maturing (Keel link).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d store: a US-GAAP recipient books her 2031 letter as donor-restricted, not spendable until January 2033; applies only if the residency or a US friends body reports under US GAAP.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the means half of row 1 (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5: weighs whether the giver can pay only when it measures). Fix: drop the $105,000-$110,000 present value, Keel arithmetic on an assumed 4.8% outside NUMBERS, never printed beside her $115,000.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d lead-in: under US GAAP the letter as described is an unconditional promise booked in 2031; any unspent-money clause is never worded as a condition on the building (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5).
Sun 22 Nov: store: GASB 33's probable-of-collection gate for US public bodies; her Treasuries pass it, but a Taiwan residency's co-sponsors are unlikely to report under GASB.
Sun 22 Nov: store, feeds row 14: for a US public body one sentence in the letter (for use from 2033) moves the booking year from 2031 to 2033.
Sun 22 Nov: store; standard-setters leave a pledge's reliability to the allowance, the split Q200-001 and row 9 draw; Basis for Conclusions, not the rule.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the honest date adopted in ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5: committed in writing in 2031, paid in January 2033; never that the figure sits on anyone's books in 2031 (four books, four answers).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, how co-sponsors keep checking (aha test 9): the paper test asks only verifiable, and hers can be checked against a statement of the named fund; the report suggests a statement, never requires one.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d's one parallel, corrected at source: Lehman Brothers Holdings' own pledge to Spelman (17 Oct 2007), a company's promise from its future business, never a pledge from a fortune (overrides H7-070's frame).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d parallel's detail: a five-year partnership, so the promise rested on the parent's next five years; the foundation stayed outside the bankruptcy, but never say it kept paying Spelman (not in the article).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the $3 million of $10 million read in the 2010 Chronicle article itself (Q200-006 and H7-070 read mirrors); the References entry for the figure; quotation mode, so S 4.
Sun 22 Nov: store, honest limit: Spelman's filings never name Lehman, so the figure stays the Chronicle's $3m of $10m; never cite the $2.24m fall in receivables as the write-off.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, one clause tying the one parallel to IPS l.9: a promise paid from five more years of a business has a writer's shape (later and smaller), and the plan holds Treasuries before stating; the shape, never the scale (D4).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d clause or 3e custody line. Fix: the broker's customer accounts and the parent's pledge sat in two proceedings, so say in the same collapse, never in one bankruptcy; give the count with its date (over 135,000 by Feb 2009), never beside Q2a-022's 110,000 in ten days.
Sun 22 Nov: store, aha 8's second kind (money that existed only on a statement): JEHT's committed three-year grant to EJI, now read at source; supersedes Q2c-024.
Sun 22 Nov: aha 8's existed only on a statement (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5): Picower's $952m on its 2007 return rested on Madoff's statements; a student paper quoting the foundation's letter, so S 4.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the ACLU's $1.5m from JEHT and Picower over four years; one article's figures.
Sun 22 Nov: aha 8 and 3e's custody limit (ARGUMENT_TREE cites row 25): Madoff's statements named Treasuries never bought, so held means held at a real broker and custodian; extends Q65-023.
Sun 22 Nov: store, the counter-cases behind row 27: paid or truly funded promises held in 2008; Shapiro's and Wachovia's are statements made at the time, later payment unchecked.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, aha 8's wording adopted in ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5: in every failed pledge read the money was expected later or existed only on a statement; say pledges read (four, all 2008), never every failed pledge.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d and 3e, kills only those two could stop it (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5): by 2031 a default remains, plus an early fund end while cash earns nothing ($4,589 at most on the top, NUMBERS 3, from her flexibility), her death, a dispute and a broker delay; two lists (card Q109).

Sun 22 Nov: store, pedigree for the estate line: Allegheny enforced a pledge payable from an estate five to two, with a dissent; the pledge's own law stays outside the case (rows 30-31 carry the use; Q77-007 the holding).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the reason for an estate line: gift offices write off a dead donor's pledge unless an estate pays (BGSU, Colorado College, CSUSB, read in extract).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, a seventh part of the letter for the writers to weigh (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5): this promise binds my estate, the wording gift agreements use (UVA, an Indiana form); it costs her nothing, since the Treasuries sit in her estate either way.
Sun 22 Nov: store or one clause in 3d: a builder asks for named assets behind gift money; always a 2018 draft for public review and the sponsor's guarantee, never a donor rule (Q43-045 stands).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d store: a matching funder may count only irrevocable pledges payable before substantial completion, so the letter says payable January 2033 plainly; one redacted ruling read through a mirror.
Sun 22 Nov: store behind row 15: verifiable, not verified, so gift offices never check a donor's means; a forum post, not guidance.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, the team's sentence before her words, adopted in ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5: held is why it will be paid, signed is why it can be counted; supersedes Q200-030's owned wording; $115,000 is the figure on today's figures.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a, one clause after the forward-rate reason (SYNTHESES lead's read, item 3): a chance below 100 fits only someone refilled, and the case bars a refill for the payments. Fix: each standard below 100 we read, never every professional standard; the case bars, never she has none; re-date the FDIC figure; Kelly a clause; never in 3f. Carries Q218-009.

Sun 22 Nov: repeats aha 2 (2.3, the order of purchase; lead's read item 4: never beside it), merged into Q206-029; what travels as aha 2's second sentence if room: the promise sets the book's size, her career its order, her taste two numbers (most, half); Tobin and Kimball in References; never optimal, never beta.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.0 or Table 2's note where the 0.5% margin is defined, one clause (cold test 10 against the RBA's slot before any 3c use): a money fund's half percent let a loss hide under $1.00, hers is cut first and rounded down; the rule of 2008; the margin is the 0.5% alone, about 2% in all is the room under the top.

Sun 22 Nov: one point with SE-2 and SB-1 (lead's read item 4), merged into Q150-024: each uncertain source counted at a safe lower bound, so nothing spare is the design; nothing spare only with the fee and the 0.5% fund costs ($1,177 without, NUMBERS 2); pedigree, bond readers know haircuts.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e, the frame around the gilt crisis. Fix: its guard keeps D20's gilt sentence, which ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 6 (card Q214) now bans: never broke fastest or no pension promise broke, use Branch 6's words; bought with cash holds from January 2028; German insurers unnamed.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e writers' frame, one risk per sentence with who can act and who covers it (voice round 13). Fix: add card Q213 row 28's her death before January 2033 (her estate) and a dispute; keep the two lists apart (card Q109); swaps unsized; never nobody can make the plan sell.

Sun 22 Nov: Table 2's note, one line beside Q210-030's rule: promises rest on holdings, history only sets limits; the 585-month replay shapes sizing by rejecting forwards; Wilks to the store; no odds from overlapping windows (D7).

Sun 22 Nov: 2.0 or 3a's why-zero sentence, one clause: for a holder counted on dated payments long Treasuries are the riskless asset (Campbell and Viceira) and waiting cash the risky one, so the standard counts it at nothing; pedigree beside D13, never on a fund's payout, never TIPS.

Sun 22 Nov: same root as SG-1 (the case bars outside money for the payments; lead's read item 4: say it once), merged into Q218-001; what travels to 3b if room: fair at market and worth more to her, since the case bars any offset, beside D15's gives up; worth more is utility, never a NUMBERS figure.

Sun 22 Nov: the thread table (ARGUMENT_TREE section 5): 2.3 plants the deposit's order, 3a pays with over-funding; new is that forward rates missed most in downturns, so the zero count is the depression case; says aha 2 and aha 5 once each, never a third aha; about three-quarters only at today's rates.

Sun 22 Nov: the close, one plain sentence in Caplet's register or none (cold test against IPS l.19). Fix: say the ten, a base of the residency's budget, depend on no share price, never that a downturn cannot make residents the last donor (stipends rest on the whole budget); no outside name, never in Laura's words.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c one clause or Table 3 row 5's note, answering why the move has a date, not a trigger: only the half promised to no one may wait for a recovery; survivorship authors in References; the RBA stays 3c's parallel.

Sun 22 Nov: repeats aha 8 (owned versus signed), merged into Q200-030 (Q213-035 now holds the corrected wording); what travels to WORDS: never paid or settled for held Treasuries, since FAS 88 counts no settlement while the decision can be reversed (Q186-011).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d's currency clause and 3b, one unnamed clause (D9): no capital-grant rule we read moves with an exchange rate, so her US-dollar figure is the norm and keeping its NT$ value whole a capped intention from her flexibility; IDA to Table 3 row 7's note or the store; NT$ figures with their day.

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 rows 16-18: Lehman's $10m was Lehman Brothers Holdings' own five-year pledge to Spelman, to be paid from the bank's future business, never a pledge from a donor's own fortune; reword the lead as a pledge fails with whoever made it and keep Duke, Otterbein and FTX; 3d's parallel and aha 8 cite Q213-016 to Q213-018.

Sun 22 Nov: override, now verified at source by card Q213 row 22 (EJI, 9 Jan 2009: grants committed for the next three years, nearly 25% of its budget; Chronicle, 9 Apr 2009: a three-year $1.5m grant); status stays merged, now into its verified twin Q213-022, since JEHT's money existed only on Madoff's statements (aha 8's second kind), not H7-070's pledge from future business.

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 verdict 5 and row 28: the IPS's two reasons change the plan; they are not the only ways her figure can fail (card Q109). By 2031 a Treasury default remains, and so do an early end of the late-2032 fund while cash earns nothing (at most $4,589 short on the top, NUMBERS 3, from her flexibility), her death before January 2033, a dispute and a broker delay; never the one remaining reason or the one thing that would stop it.

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 verdict 5 and row 28: true that after January 2028 only one of the two reasons to change can still happen, but a 2031 promise has more ways to fall short than a default: an early fund end while cash earns nothing (at most $4,589 on the top, NUMBERS 3), her death, a dispute, a broker delay; never one exit, and keep the two lists apart (card Q109).

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 verdict 5: never from 2031 one exit remains as what co-sponsors are told could stop her figure; a default is the one reason to change left, while an early fund end while cash earns nothing, her death, a dispute and a broker delay remain (Q213 row 28); the IPS's barring a US default is quoted only as the IPS's words, never attached to the report's own strong words (Book 19).

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 row 28, which supersedes it: never Laura's list has two items; the missed deposit is spent by 2031, but a default, fund costs past the margin (about $118 off the top per 0.1%, NUMBERS 3), an early fund end while cash earns nothing ($4,589 at most), her death, a dispute and a broker delay remain; keep the two lists apart.

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 verdict 5: the critique's only a US default lowers it is wrong; say she cannot withdraw a stated figure (her letter has no exit, Q213-003), while fund costs past its cover (about 3% for the bottom, NUMBERS 8u) or a fund event could leave a figure short, met from her flexibility; the venture analogy otherwise stands.

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 verdict 5 and row 28: never tell co-sponsors any surprise can only be upward; below a stated figure sit a default, fund costs past the margin, an early fund end while cash earns nothing (at most $4,589 on the top, NUMBERS 3, from her flexibility), her death and a broker delay; anything above the top goes to her flexibility, never a raised range.

Sun 22 Nov: override adding a second fix from card Q213 verdict 5 (card Q109): never only two reasons can touch the ten; the two reasons change the plan and what could still break a payment is a separate list; Friday's fix stands: five of the ten are iBond fund shares, so say Treasuries and Treasury funds, walled off from the building's money.

Sun 22 Nov: override from card Q213 verdict 5: never every event that could ever excuse her; the two exits are reasons to change the plan, and her death, a dispute, an early fund end while cash earns nothing and a broker delay can still leave a stated figure unpaid or short (Q213 row 28); Friday's fix stands: the two reasons are not market prices, never cannot, and a missed deposit can be her choice.
